title: Sycamore: Ancient Sycamore Maples You Can Visit
meta_description: Nobody plants a sycamore on purpose any more. Tolpuddle's, where six labourers met in 1833 to form a union, is about 340 years old.
intro: Nobody plants a sycamore on purpose any more. It seeds itself into gutters, railway banks and any gap it can find across northern Europe, grows fast, and gets cut down long before it becomes anything, which is precisely what makes an old one worth looking up at. Glasgow's Darnley Sycamore is put at 450 to 500 years, exceptional for a species that rarely passes 400, and it carries the name of Mary, Queen of Scots' husband on a story from 1565. On the village green at Tolpuddle in Dorset, six farm labourers met under a sycamore in 1833 to form a union and were transported to Australia for it; the tree is about 340 years old and 6.06 metres round. Copenhagen's is the thickest tree inside Assistens cemetery and the least exotic species in it. Edinburgh's grows sideways out of solid rock at the start of a riverside walkway.
